# Syllabus {- #syllabus}

**STAT 531 – Data Analysis Using Statistical Packages**

## Objective {-}

This course introduces students to the use of statistical packages for the analysis of data. It gives hands-on experience in analysing research data and is useful to students of all disciplines.

## Course content and where to find it {-}

| Unit | Syllabus topics | Chapters |
|:----:|:----------------|:---------|
| I | Use of software packages for summarisation and tabulation of data; descriptive statistics; graphical representation of data; exploratory data analysis | \@ref(introduction)–\@ref(eda) |
| II | Fitting and testing the goodness of fit of discrete and continuous probability distributions; testing of hypothesis based on large-sample test statistics; testing of hypothesis using chi-square, *t* and *F* statistics | \@ref(distributions)–\@ref(small-sample) |
| III | Concept of analysis of variance and covariance of data for single-factor, multi-factor, one-way and multi-classified experiments; contrast analysis; multiple comparisons | \@ref(anova-crd)–\@ref(ancova) |
| IV | Analysis of mixed models; estimation of variance components; testing the significance of contrasts; correlation and regression including multiple regression | \@ref(mixed-models)–\@ref(regression) |
| V | Discriminant function; factor analysis; principal component analysis; analysis of time-series data; fitting of non-linear models | \@ref(pca)–\@ref(time-series-analysis-using-r) |

## Unit I {-}

Use of software packages for: summarisation and tabulation of data; descriptive statistics; graphical representation of data; exploratory data analysis.

## Unit II {-}

Fitting and testing the goodness of fit of discrete and continuous probability distributions; testing of hypothesis based on large-sample test statistics; testing of hypothesis using chi-square, *t* and *F* statistics.

## Unit III {-}

Concept of analysis of variance and covariance of data for single-factor, multi-factor, one-way and multi-classified experiments; contrast analysis; multiple comparisons.

## Unit IV {-}

Analysis of mixed models; estimation of variance components; testing the significance of contrasts; correlation and regression including multiple regression.

## Unit V {-}

Discriminant function; factor analysis; principal component analysis; analysis of time-series data; fitting of non-linear models.
